Choosing between Coupang (NYSE:CPNG) and MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) means weighing South Korea's logistics king against Latin America's fintech and retail giant to see which offers better value for everyday investors.

Both companies dominate their respective regions through integrated ecosystems that provide commerce, payments, and delivery. While Coupang focuses on extreme density and speed in South Korea and Taiwan, MercadoLibre operates across 18 countries, leveraging its fintech arm to capture unbanked populations. This comparison examines their performance to determine the better buy today.

The case for Coupang

Coupang operates as a dominant force in South Korean e-commerce, offering retail, restaurant delivery, and video streaming. The company serves roughly 24.7 million active customers through brands like Eats and Play, operating within the retail stocks category. It also recently acquired luxury platform Farfetch to broaden its presence in high-end specialty retail across more than 190 countries, utilizing infrastructure from Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) to support its technology needs.

In its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, Coupang reported revenue of nearly $34.5 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 14.1% over the prior year. The company generated net income of $208.0 million, resulting in a net margin of roughly 0.6%. This performance shows steady progress compared to FY 2024, as the company scales its infrastructure and handles higher order volumes across its Rocket Delivery network.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is nearly 1.0x, which measures a company's ability to cover short-term liabilities with short-term assets. The debt-to-equity ratio is 1.0x, indicating that total debt equals shareholders' equity. For the fiscal year, free cash flow was approximately $522.0 million. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 26.8% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back to cash flow.

The case for MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre functions as the primary e-commerce and fintech ecosystem in Latin America through its Mercado Libre and Mercado Pago platforms. The business connects nearly 89 million unique active buyers across 18 countries, providing essential services like logistics through Mercado Envios. It relies on global cloud providers, primarily Amazon and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL), to manage its massive digital transactions and marketplace operations across the region.

title: Amazon Fuel Up Fridays Returns: How Prime Members Can Save Big at the Gas Pump
detail:
Amazon Fuel Up Fridays Returns: How Prime Members Can Save Big at the Gas Pump
Caitlyn Moorhead
Sat, October 10, 2026 at 10:00 AM MST 4 min read
AMZN
Trade AMZN on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Getty Images

If you've been driving past the gas station on fumes and wincing at the price per gallon, Amazon just gave Prime members a very good reason to stop and fill up on Fridays.

Just in time for the holiday season, Fuel Up Fridays is back, and the savings this year are double what members get year-round. Here's everything you need to know.

Quick Take: What Exactly Is Amazon Fuel Up Fridays?

According to Amazon's official announcement, Fuel Up Fridays returned Oct. 2, through Jan. 29, 2027, and gives Prime members $0.20 off per gallon on one fuel purchase every Friday at participating locations.

That's double the everyday Prime fuel discount of $0.10 per gallon that members already enjoy year-round at more than 7,500 bp, Amoco and participating ampm and Thorntons locations across the U.S.

How To Activate Your Savings

Savings in this economy, especially on gas, can go a long way toward making ends meet. Fortunately, setting up the discount is a one-time process and takes about two minutes, according to Amazon. Just follow these steps:

Visit amazon.com/fuelsavings to activate the offer.

Connect your Amazon account to a free Earnify account with BP (this only needs to be done once).

Find your nearest participating station using the free Earnify app store locator.

Redeem at the pump by entering your phone number or linked payment method (or you can use the Earnify app to select your location and pump directly).

That's all it entails, and once activated, the discount applies automatically every time you fuel up at a qualifying location. To put the full-year savings in perspective, the year-round $0.10 per gallon discount alone saves the average Prime member nearly $70 per year, which is almost half the cost of an annual Prime membership.

Fuel Up Fridays stack on top of that baseline, pushing total fuel savings even higher through the end of January, and the proof is in the returns.

The Family Hack That Can Stack Your Savings

If you share a household with another Prime member, get ready to watch the savings pile up, as two adults in the same household can share a Prime membership at no additional cost through Amazon Family, and each member can make a separate fuel transaction. That means your household can effectively double Fuel Up Friday savings by making two separate fill-ups on the same Friday.

Keep in mind that the only catch is that both household members need separate Earnify accounts, and each must complete their own fuel transaction. For a household with two drivers filling up every Friday for the next few months, that's 17 weeks of double discounts, plus a meaningful chunk of change over the holiday driving season.
